newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen falling at the open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen falling at the open.

text.p: Toronto stocks were expected to open lower on Tuesday after several sessions of strong gains on both sides of the border.

An expected tumble in Bre-X Minerals Ltd shares, due to resume trading at the open after being halted when a report revealed that the company's Busang property was in fact a fraud, would add to the downward pressure, traders said.
"(Equities) are going down. It's time," said one trader.
"Bre-X is going to open and it's going to dive, so that's going to have an impact as well," he added.
On Monday, the Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index gained 43.82 points to close to 6150.73.

The preliminary estimate of average weekly earnings for Canadian workers in all industries except agriculture and fishing rose 3.6 percent in February from a year earlier to a seasonally adjusted C$598.72, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday. From the month before, earnings rose 0.3 percent.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast that average weekly earnings would rise by 3.9 percent, year on year, after a 4.1 percent rise in January.

* Norcen Energy Resources Ltd and Basic Petroleum International Ltd said on Tuesday they reached a deal under which Norcen would offer US$40 a share for up to 97.5 percent of Basic or a total of US$303 million.
